relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with two ALDH5A1 variants and confirmed SSADH deficiency: "revealed two variants for the ALDH5A1 gene".
method_note: Read by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person (single unnamed patient, label 'patient'). Parents are mentioned only as reporters of history, with no testing or features, so no relative rows. Zygosity not stated (two ALDH5A1 variants found, phase/compound heterozygosity not stated) and variant type not stated: both left not reported. No parental testing reported. Karyotype, array CGH, subtelomeric, fragile X, Prader-Willi and Angelman studies were negative: genetic tests, not phenotypes, so no feature rows. The 1.5T brain MRI at 22 months was reported as normal, while a later 3T MRI (age not stated) showed bilateral globus pallidus T2 hyperintensity and mild cerebellar vermis atrophy; recorded as an excluded 'abnormal brain MRI' row limited to that scan (excludes nothing more specific) plus observed rows for the later findings; not treated as a contradiction because they are different scans at different ages. EEG checklist item left not reported because the authors call the slow/sharp theta pattern 'not clearly pathological'; the EEG finding itself is a phenotypic_features row. 'Inability to maintain a conversation' was listed under behaviour; speech/language checklist left not reported. Hypotonia, sleep awakenings, motor deficit and gait ataxia were transient; recorded as observed with detail. Vigabatrin is discussed only in general, not as this patient's treatment. Vital status not explicitly stated.
